source.scope: Abstract/title/keywords variants reconciled with the current manuscript (measurement-audit framing)
source.evidenceScope: WVS Trend File 1981-2022: 442,026 respondents, 305 country-years scanned; constructs Z (alpha 0.8187), C (0.3482), D (-1.2285), S (uncomputable)

selectedTitle: Measurement Validity Before Model Geometry: A Reproducible Audit of Bounded Response Models
selectedSubtitle: Composite Constructs, Support Limits, and an Honest Model Comparison for Country Panels
selectionRationale: The balanced variant is selected because it leads with the protocol contribution, states the construct failures and the baseline loss without burying them, and names the sample precisely. It stays legible for an indicator-methodology desk while carrying the evidence a data-society editor expects.

abstractVariants.label: Conservative
abstractVariants.editorUse: Use when the editor values a narrow, fully checkable methods claim and low desk-reject risk.
abstractVariants.text: Applied work on bounded social indicators routinely reports model fit before establishing that the constructs being modelled are measurable. This paper reverses that order and reports what the reversal cost. Three composite constructs underpinning a published bounded nonlinear model of country-panel belief intensity were re-derived from item-level World Values Survey data: cultural intensity reached Cronbach alpha = 0.35 and social atomization alpha = -1.23, so neither measures a single dimension, and social support could not be computed in any country-year. In the published panel the outcome was also an exact rescaling of the cultural-intensity predictor (corr = 1.0), which made every reported out-of-sample metric algebraically guaranteed. On the rebuilt panel of 207 complete-case country-years across 83 countries (1990-2023), a saturating model reaches leave-one-country-out R2 = 0.10, below the 0.20 of an ordinary linear regression on identical rows and folds. Interpretation is descriptive and non-causal.

abstractVariants.label: Balanced
abstractVariants.editorUse: Default. Leads with the protocol contribution, keeps the negative results visible, and states the sample precisely.
abstractVariants.text: Measurement precedes modelling: a coefficient on a composite construct is interpretable only if that construct measures something. We turn that principle into an executable audit protocol with four hard gates - construct reliability, item overlap, design-matrix rank and a baseline comparison - and apply it to a published bounded nonlinear framework for country-panel belief intensity. Three of four candidate composites fail. Cultural intensity (alpha = 0.35) and social atomization (alpha = -1.23) are not unidimensional; social support is uncomputable from the harmonised source. In the original panel the outcome was additionally an exact rescaling of a predictor (corr = 1.0). The rebuilt panel contains 207 complete-case country-years across 83 countries (1990-2023). With the surviving constructs, the saturating map reaches leave-one-country-out R2 = 0.10 against 0.20 for a linear regression on the same rows, and fixed-coefficient country-out validation is negative in every tier. The contribution is the reproducible audit, not the response surface: every gate fails on the original panel and each failure is regenerable from committed artifacts. Interpretation remains descriptive and non-causal.

abstractVariants.label: High-impact but bounded
abstractVariants.editorUse: Use only where a methodological correction is itself the news; strongest for indicator and data-society venues.
abstractVariants.text: A published class of bounded response-surface models for country-panel belief intensity rests on composite constructs that were never tested for measurability. Auditing them on item-level World Values Survey data withdraws three of four: cultural intensity (alpha = 0.35) and social atomization (alpha = -1.23) fail unidimensionality, and social support cannot be computed at all. Worse, the original panel's outcome was an exact rescaling of the cultural-intensity predictor (corr = 1.0), so its near-unity R2 was arithmetic rather than empirical. Rebuilding the panel to 207 complete-case country-years across 83 countries (1990-2023) leaves a saturating model that does not beat a linear baseline (leave-one-country-out R2 = 0.10 versus 0.20) and whose fixed-coefficient predictions are worse than the held-out country means. We report this as the finding. The reusable contribution is a four-gate audit protocol - reliability, item overlap, design rank, baseline comparison - that any composite-indicator pipeline can adopt, and that would have blocked the original model at release.
